newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra mulls Telstra preference shares.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra mulls Telstra preference shares.

text.p: Australian Communications Minister Richard Alston said on Friday the government was still considering Independent Senator Brian Harradine's proposal to sell redeemable preference shares in Telstra Corp.
Harradine offered the proposal in September as an alternative to the government's planned partial privatisation of its telecommunications corporation.
"Yes, we're still having discussions with Senator Harradine," Alston told reporters when asked whether he was still considering that proposal.
The government wants to sell one-third of Telstra.
Preference shares are assets part-way between equity and debt and their dividends are normally fixed.
If the company is wound up, the holder has preference over ordinary shareholders and redeemable preference shares can be redeemed for value, under specified conditions.
The government's plan to sell Telstra for A$8.0 billion relies on the support of Harradine and another Independent senator, Mal Colston.
All other non-government senators oppose the plan and the government is two votes short of a majority in the upper house Senate. -- Canberra Bureau 61-6 273 2730
